verdict.rationale: Cursor's own agent writes and modifies code and tests the features it builds. Its marketing shows an agent updating Node.js version constraints across a project, which touches dependency updates, and the SDK cookbook lists CI auto-fix bots. The four named chores are not each documented as agent capabilities, though: test-writing is only implied by building and testing features, and lint-fixing and merge-conflict resolution are never mentioned. missing for 10: explicit documentation of the agent authoring tests, fixing lint errors, resolving merge conflicts, a documented dependency-upgrade workflow, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the agent write tests, fix lint errors, resolve merge conflicts, and update dependencies for me

citations.quote: Agents use their own computers to build, test, and demo features end to end for you to review.
